sermon.title: Leviathan and Lucifer
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that Leviathan in Isaiah 27 and Job 41 pictures Satan, “king over all the children of pride,” and that Jesus destroyed his power over believers. He then teaches on Lucifer in Isaiah 14, the stars of God, angels and the destroyer, and the believer’s authority, ending with the saints taking the kingdom and Jesus as the Lion of the tribe of Judah.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: at about 18:56 he reads “1 Corinthians 11:14” (Satan masquerading as an angel of light); that wording is 2 Corinthians 11:14, shown here. At about 15:36 the caption reads “Hebrews 24,” taken as Hebrews 2:14. At about 36:30 he reads “Daniel 7:8,” but the words match Daniel 7:18, shown here. In the Revelation 9:11 passage (about 30:27) the Greek name was garbled in the captions and is marked [unclear]; the Hebrew name Abaddon is as he says it. “Shilo” in the captions was taken as Sheol and “tears” as tares. Passages on other religions, Israel and politics (about 38:00–45:00), on atheists, and on demon possession reflect his views as spoken.

chunks.section_question: What is Leviathan, and can anyone overcome him? (Isaiah 27:1, Job 41:1–10)
chunks.short_answer: He says Leviathan is a serpent: in Isaiah 27:1 the Lord “will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent,” “the twisted serpent.” Turning to Job 41, he says “any hope of overcoming Leviathan is false” and “man cannot defeat this snake.” He says God hides mysteries by switching between the natural and the spiritual, and “only the Holy Ghost can reveal them to you.”
chunks.text:
We’re going to ask ourselves, what is Leviathan? Okay, and we, of course, will go to the Bible to find out what Leviathan is. Uh, they made a movie about it, and this has nothing to do with that movie. Isaiah 27, verse 1: “In that day,” now remember that “day” is mentioned over and over and over and over in Isaiah, speaking of the future events of God. “In that day the Lord,” the Lord is Jesus Christ, “with his severe sword, great and strong, will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent.” So Leviathan is a serpent. Okay. “Leviathan the twisted serpent.” Again, Leviathan is a serpent, “and he will slay the reptile that is in the sea.” So we got a bunch of snakes being talked about here, and, uh, we find that Leviathan is a serpent, okay, a snake.

Then we’re going to go to Job 41, where God himself, talking to Job, gives us great details about Leviathan, thorough details. Job 41: “Any hope of overcoming Leviathan is false.” That’s a false hope. Man cannot defeat this snake. “One shall be overwhelmed at the very sight of him.” He’s just going to be terrorized just by looking at this snake. “No one’s so fierce that he would dare stir up Leviathan.” No human being got enough courage, enough military strength, the warrior, to overcome and stir up Leviathan. And then God switches. Now remember, Isaiah would be talking about a nation or an Israel, and then he would switch to the future. Okay, and this is how God hid his mysteries in the Bible, and only the Holy Ghost can reveal them to you. You can’t go to college and get this stuff, it’s not an intellectual thing, it is a spiritual thing. All right.

chunks.section_question: Why does God use Leviathan to ask who can stand against him? (Job 41:10–29)
chunks.short_answer: He says God uses this “overwhelming snake” to ask “who then is able to stand against me?”, because Job “was righteous until he blamed God for his problems.” He describes Leviathan’s fire, breath and scales and the failure of swords, spears and arrows, saying “nothing can touch this guy.”
chunks.text:
So God uses this overwhelming snake to turn it around and say, “Who then is able to stand against me?” Because that’s what Job had done. He had blamed God. Job was righteous until he blamed God for his problems. He accused God. And so, “Who then is able to stand against me?” If you can’t, you guys can’t conquer this snake, then who has the guts to stand up against me? Amen. So it’s, it’s a good illustration, and remember, Jesus said, “I speak to you of earthly things so you can understand heavenly things.” All right, now he goes on, verse 19: “Out of Leviathan’s mouth go burning lights, sparks of fire shoot out, smoke goes out of his nose as from a boiling pot and a burning bush.”

It rushes. The Bible says that he caused the depths of the sea to boil when he opened his mouth with fire. His breath kindles coals, a flame goes out of his mouth. Verse 26: “Though the sword reaches him, it cannot avail.” Can’t pierce this snake. “Nor does a spear, a dart, a javelin,” and back in verse 7, even, I passed over it because I wanted to stay on the topic back there, the harpoon, the javelin, the dart, the spear cannot pierce his skin. His scales are so tight and so hard, nothing can touch this guy. “He regards iron as straw.” You know, you throw a war axe at him and it just breaks like a straw. “Bronze is rotten wood.” The arrow cannot make him flee. So he has used up the weapons of a man. A man’s weapons cannot hurt this reptile, this serpent. “Slingstones become like stubble to him.” They sling them at him and they just break like a clod of dirt. “Darts are regarded as straw.” They throw a spear at him, just like throwing a piece of straw. That’s how vicious this animal was, this snake.

chunks.section_question: Is Leviathan a real creature, and who is king over the children of pride? (Job 41:33–34)
chunks.short_answer: He says Leviathan, talked about “five times in the Old Testament,” is “the natural snake that can breathe out fire,” and tells hearers not to believe “versions of the Bible that say it’s a crocodile.” He says the “switch” comes at the end of Job 41, where this snake is “king over all the children of pride,” illustrating that “nobody can stand against him.”
chunks.text:
That Isaiah said God would destroy in that day. What day, and what would God do? Destroy him. Okay. “He laughs at the threat of javelins.” Now, you got to remember, all water animals survived the flood. You say, “Well, we know dinosaurs got wiped out back there.” Well, any monster in the sea would be fine. So get away from that. God does know what he’s talking about, all right. Now, natural scientists don’t believe that, but God is literally talking about, and Leviathan’s talked about five times in the Old Testament, five times, and God is using the natural snake that can breathe out fire, nothing can oppose him, to illustrate. And don’t believe these, these, um, versions of the Bible that say it’s a crocodile or something. Just accept it the way God said it, okay? And that’s the way he’s saying it, and it’s important that you do, because the spiritual truth lines up with this, all right.

Verse 33: “On earth there is nothing like him, which is made without fear.” This snake fears nothing. “He beholds every high thing,” and here comes the switch from the natural snake. “He is king over all the children of pride.” He is king over all. Now here’s the switch. Now he’s switching. This snake cannot be king over humans at all, can it? They can’t rule them, can’t have any effect on them. And so he’s using this terrible creature to illustrate how people cannot stand before God, and like it was said this morning, nothing is impossible with God. He will save, he will deliver, he will, nothing can stop him. Okay, he is a Savior, he is a Deliverer, he is a Healer, and nobody has authority to stand against God, the Lord Jesus Christ. Is that an amen? Yeah. So he’s using this bad snake to illustrate how powerful Jesus Christ is, okay, that nobody can stand against him. And then he’s using this snake to illustrate that there is a king over, in the spirit world, over all the children of pride. Now, the word “pride” there in the Hebrew has a two-fold meaning. It is a pride of lion cubs, a family of lions.

He cites 1 Peter 5:8, “your adversary the Devil is as a roaring lion,” and says “understanding Leviathan helps us understand Satan” and that “people are so proud they won’t bow their need to God.”
chunks.text:

The angels and the elders are all kneeling, and a number that can’t be numbered are kneeling, and you’re going to stand there and say, “Huh, no”? Now it’s pride. Pride comes before a fall. Yes. chunks.section_question: Who are Satan’s children? (John 12:31, Ephesians 2:2, Matthew 13:38, Psalm 10:4, John 3:19–20)
chunks.short_answer: Citing John 12:31, Ephesians 2:2 and Matthew 13:38, he says Satan is “a ruler over this world” with children, and “we know them because they disobey the word of God.” He says those who “reject Christ and reject the word” are “our biggest opposition,” that they do not admit their wrong, and that people who accept “a Jesus that does not reveal their sins” have “the wrong Jesus.”
chunks.text:
Now, Satan has children of pride, a lion’s cubs, he has a family, he has children. Ephesians 2:2: “The prince and power of the air, the spirit that now works in the children of disobedience.” So Satan is a king of the air, this earth, and he has children, and we know them because they disobey the word of God. Okay, they’re under the control of Satan, they follow Satan’s rules. Got it? All right, Matthew 13:38: “The tares are the children of the wicked one. The enemy that sowed them is the Devil.” See, he has an offspring, and those offspring of his, those children that reject Christ and reject the word, are our biggest opposition in this earth. They oppose us constantly. Psalm, uh, 10:4: “The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God.”

So, see, these are children of the wicked one, and they’re wicked because of their pride. They will not admit their wrong, that’s pride. They will not ask Jesus to forgive them of their sins and come into their life and make them a light to the world. See, they want to sin. The reason atheists don’t want to believe there’s a God is they want to sin. I mean, I would tell my atheist brother that, you know, yeah, it’s, you just want to do what you want to do, because when you come to Christ, he will reveal your sins. That’s what John chapter 3 says, isn’t that right? That their sins might be made known. They come to Christ, they won’t come to Christ lest their sins be made known. And that’s why people, and people that accept a Jesus that does not reveal their sins have the wrong Jesus. Now that was a good statement. You know, there, there, there are people out there that believe in Jesus, but their description of Jesus and definition of Jesus is not the definition of Jesus in the Bible. And you got to, you see, you got to find the source of things. You know, a lot of people out there say, “I believe in Jesus.” What Jesus do you believe in? Hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: Did Jesus destroy Satan’s power over believers? (Hebrews 2:14, Romans 16:20)
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus “destroyed Satan” on the cross: reading Hebrews 2:14, he says Christ “reduced him to zero, neutral, over anyone that will believe in Christ.” He says learning this “revolutionized my life,” that Satan “has no jurisdiction over me” and “all he can do is ask me to do something bad,” and citing Romans 16:20 he says “I need him under my feet now.”
chunks.text:
And so we see then that the Devil is Leviathan, and in that day Jesus is going to destroy his power. Okay, and destroy him. We’ve got to understand that he’s already done that. When he came, Jesus destroyed Satan, and so does his people. It’s very plain, and when people get up and say that “Satan’s followed me” and “Satan did this to me,” they don’t understand the power of Christ in your life, the atonement, the deliverance that Jesus did on that cross. Okay, Hebrews 2:14: “Through death He destroyed him that had the power of death, that is, the Devil.” So when Christ died on the cross, he destroyed the power of Satan, reduced him to zero, neutral, over anyone that will believe in Christ. Yes, yes. Hallelujah.

Now, when I was a boy, you grew up in church, Satan was in control. You know, “Satan made me do this, Satan made me do that, Satan, Satan, Satan, Satan.” I learned that Satan was destroyed, it revolutionized my life. Instead of looking to Satan, I started looking to the author and finisher of my faith. “He that began a good work in me will” what? Finish it. Hallelujah. And Satan has no jurisdiction over me. None. Period. Are you there? All he can do is ask me to do something bad. He can have no power over me to make me do it. Got it? He can just suggest. Romans 16:20: “The God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet.” At the rapture? No, I don’t need him under my feet at the rapture, I need him under my feet now. And he said he would do it, what? Quickly. And so God’s people have authority over Satan in the kingdom of darkness. And as I was teaching in the home Bible study, fasting and prayer is what raises that level of authority. When you come in contact with the kingdom of darkness and demons and so forth, you have authority to control the situation. And if you go to third world countries or you go into these neighborhoods where they are really, you know, down in darkness, you better have some authority. Your little head knowledge isn’t going to work there.

chunks.section_question: Can a Christian be demon-possessed? Is Satan an angel of light? (2 Corinthians 11:14)
chunks.short_answer: He says the strong man of the house is Jesus, who “can’t be bound,” so “Christians can’t be demon-possessed” because “Jesus lives in us.” He says “much of the church world don’t understand this and they’re in bondage.” Reading that Satan “masquerades as an angel of light,” he says Satan imitates, while Jesus said “I am the light of the world.”
chunks.text:
Are you with me? Yes. Yeah, hallelujah, church. Do you understand this? Yes. Do you realize the strong man of our house is Jesus, and Jesus said that the strong man of the house can’t be bound, and so Christians can’t be demon-possessed. They can’t overpower Jesus who lives in us. See, we get that Spirit of God when we get saved, it’s different than the baptism of the Holy Ghost, but it’s still the same Spirit, and we have authority, and Jesus lives in us, and Satan cannot come in and control us. Amen. True. Now, much of the church world don’t understand this, and they’re in bondage, you know, it’s horrible.

Now, 1 Corinthians 11:14: “Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light.” Okay, he masquerades as an angel of light, he imitates. All right, he’s not an angel of light. Jesus said, “I am the light of the world,” and then Jesus turned and said, “You’re the light of the world.” See, we’re not imitators, unless we are saying we’re serving God and we’re really serving the Devil, then we become imitators. chunks.section_question: Did God create the destroyer, and what do angels do? (Isaiah 54:16, Hebrews 1:14, Revelation 12:4)
chunks.short_answer: Citing Isaiah 54:16, he says God “created the waster, the destroyer, to destroy,” and that God “cannot do evil,” so he used a destroying angel in Egypt. He says Satan “wants to rule over the church” and took “one third of the stars” with him, and that angels are “ministering spirits” who “come to strengthen you” and “encourage you.”
chunks.text:
Isaiah 54:16: “I have created the waster, the destroyer, to destroy.” Amen. Who created Satan? God did. What was his purpose in creating Satan? To do what? God, who cannot do bad, will do, and hell and the lake of fire was made for who? Satan and his angels and those who follow him. Okay. So in summation, we read that God created Lucifer, the shining one, an angel, a spirit, to destroy, as God cannot do evil. So when he slew everybody, the firstborn in Egypt, he brought in the destroying angel. He exalted his throne above the stars, the angels, ministering spirits, as it says in Hebrews 1:14, to believers. Angels are ministering spirits to believers. You have an angel, the church has angels, and if God opened their eyes, we would see them. And he wants to rule over the church, he don’t like you serving Christ, he wants you to serve him. He was cast down to earth. Revelation 12:4 says “and took one third of the stars with him.” What are the stars? Angels. He took one-third of the stars with him when he was kicked out of heaven, all right. So two-thirds of the angels stayed, messengers of the church. Do you understand that? Yes, sir. Hallelujah. So when you have an angel appears to you, why does he come? To say something. That’s what angels do. They come, and if they appear and materialize, they have a message for you, they come to minister to you.

Didn’t angels come to minister to Christ after the 40 days in the desert? Yes. Yeah, they come to strengthen you, they come to encourage you. And as we read, he will be cast down into the pit and then the lake of fire, and in the meanwhile Satan has authority to test and tempt mankind, and he has authority to destroy unbelievers and the disobedient. If I [unclear] disobey God’s word, that can destroy, it can wind up killing me, let alone destroy my family, my children, my marriage, and then my life. And Satan has that authority when you come into the authority of his kingdom. You’re coming into the kingdom of destruction. Are you there? And Jesus can literally say, set you free from his control and his power. He literally can. That’s Bible. Jesus’s death rendered Satan powerless over his church and obedient believers.

Okay, so we don’t know how long that is, but we know in Egypt they were down there 400 years under slavery to the Egyptian government, Egyptian people, until the sin of Canaan came to maturity, the Bible says came to its fullness. Then he brought them out with 10 great judgments and then gave them their promise, and they ruled over Canaan. Then, yeah. Now in our generation, Israel became a nation in 1948, very significant, important fulfillment of prophecy, because the Bible said they would become a natural nation again. And it’s no accident that there was a tremendous visitation of God in the late ‘40s, to parallel with that restoration of Israel becoming a nation. But Israel did not get control of Jerusalem for till 20 years later, 1967. Then they got control over Jerusalem, and guess what happened in 1967?

scriptures.text_nkjv: But the saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom, and possess the kingdom forever, even forever and ever.’
“I was watching; and the same horn was making war against the saints, and prevailing against them,
And they will fall by the edge of the sword, and be led away captive into all nations. And Jerusalem will be trampled by Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.

Then He said to Abram: “Know certainly that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not theirs, and will serve them, and they will afflict them four hundred years. And also the nation whom they serve I will judge; afterward they shall come out with great possessions. Now as for you, you shall go to your fathers in peace; you shall be buried at a good old age. But in the fourth generation they shall return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete.”

chunks.section_question: What does he say about Israel in 1948 and 1967, the Catholic Church and the Dome of the Rock?
chunks.short_answer: He says Israel becoming a nation and regaining Jerusalem were prophetic, and that in 1967 “God poured out his Spirit on the Catholic Church,” so “God still cares for every kind, every flavor, of believer.” He tells a story about the Dome of the Rock and says “religious people really worship natural things,” while “we can go right to the throne of Jesus.” These are his claims and are not verified here.
chunks.text:
God poured out his Spirit on the Catholic Church, after he’d already poured out his Spirit on all these other denominations. 1967, he poured out the Holy Ghost, speaking in tongues, worshiping God, the power of God on the Catholics. And so we got to take note that God still cares for every kind, every flavor, of believer, doesn’t he? It doesn’t matter if you’re Orthodox, Episcopalian, a Catholic, a Baptist, or whatever. God cares for his people that believe in him, and he made it very plain in the ‘60s, very plain. Now, Israel gave control of the Dome of the Rock back to Jordan’s Muslims to keep peace. You say, “What’s that got to do with anything?” Well, the [unclear] built over the, over that rock, that rock is the foundation stone in the old temple. And religious people really worship natural things. Have you ever noticed that? Jerusalem, a rock in the old temple, it was, it was the foundation stone in the old temple, and when the Muslim leader had the engineers to build the new, they build it, they left the foundation stone outside the new building, and so he killed him after he found out. So the eastern wall, the Dome of the Rock, is on the outside of it, and the Muslims built a mosque there, and Israel, to keep peace.

Because when Jordan had Jerusalem, they wouldn’t let the Israelites in to worship. In this natural city, that’s just beyond understanding, why we want to worship in Jerusalem, the Dome of the Rock, the Wailing Wall, when we can go right to the throne of Jesus. Amen. We don’t have to make any journey or anything, I can just get on my knees in my bedroom and bam, there’s the throne of God. But religious people do funny things. Yeah, they really do. They really do funny things. So we can be looking forward to something happening to that Dome of the Rock, all right, just like we can be looking forward to something happening to God’s glorious church before he raptures us, becoming a glorious church, a mature bride ready for the coming of Christ, a church that the gates of hell is not prevailing against. Why? Because Jesus already, in his death, put Satan powerless to those who believe.

chunks.text: He already quickly put Satan under your feet. Quickly. As a believer he’ll do it quickly, and there’s coming a day when he’s going to work on Satan right here on earth, exalt his church, and bring in a great harvest. Amen. So Lucifer is the imitator. Jesus is the real, life. Lucifer and Leviathan are a lion without teeth, without claws, without power. Jesus is the Lion of the tribe of Judah, and he’s the King of kings and the Lord of lords. Amen. Hallelujah. So let’s give Jesus a big hand for his work on the cross. Yeah.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But one of the elders said to me, “Do not weep. Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has prevailed to open the scroll and to loose its seven seals.”
And He has on His robe and on His thigh a name written: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS.

faqs.question: What does he say “that day” in Isaiah means?
faqs.answer: He says the word “day” is mentioned “over and over and over and over in Isaiah, speaking of the future events of God.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: In that day the LORD with His severe sword, great and strong, Will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan that twisted serpent; And He will slay the reptile that is in the sea.

faqs.question: Who does he say can reveal the mysteries hidden in the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says God hid his mysteries by switching between the natural and the spiritual, and “only the Holy Ghost can reveal them to you.”

faqs.question: What does he say about Leviathan and the flood?
faqs.answer: He says “all water animals survived the flood,” so “any monster in the sea would be fine.” This is his explanation and is not verified here.

faqs.question: What does he say about pride?
faqs.answer: He says Satan “has a pride,” and that “pride comes before a fall.” He says people are so proud they “won’t bow their need to God.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Pride goes before destruction, And a haughty spirit before a fall.

faqs.question: Why does he say atheists do not want to believe in God?
faqs.answer: He says atheists do not want to believe because “they want to sin.” This is his statement about a group, not a verified claim.

faqs.question: What does he say about people who blame Satan?
faqs.answer: He says that when people say “Satan’s followed me and Satan did this to me,” they “don’t understand the power of Christ in your life.”

faqs.question: What does he mean that Satan has no jurisdiction over him?
faqs.answer: He says “Satan has no jurisdiction over me,” and that “all he can do is ask me to do something bad.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Inasmuch then as the children have partaken of flesh and blood, He Himself likewise shared in the same, that through death He might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,

faqs.question: Does he say a Christian can be demon-possessed?
faqs.answer: He says “Christians can’t be demon-possessed” because “Jesus lives in us.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Or how can one enter a strong man’s house and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong man? And then he will plunder his house.

faqs.question: What difference does he draw between Jesus as Savior and as Lord?
faqs.answer: He says “there’s a difference between Jesus the Savior and Jesus the Lord,” and that a slave of Jesus says “Yes, Master.”

faqs.question: What does he say the name Lucifer means?
faqs.answer: He says Lucifer means “the shining one.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “How you are fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! How you are cut down to the ground, You who weakened the nations!

faqs.question: Where does he say sin begins?
faqs.answer: He says sin “doesn’t begin down here,” and that “the heart’s the head, the mind.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For you have said in your heart: ‘I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God; I will also sit on the mount of the congregation On the farthest sides of the north; I will ascend above the heights of the clouds, I will be like the Most High.’

faqs.question: Who does he say created Satan?
faqs.answer: He says “God did,” and that God “cannot do evil.” He says hell and the lake of fire were made for “Satan and his angels and those who follow him.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “Behold, I have created the blacksmith Who blows the coals in the fire, Who brings forth an instrument for his work; And I have created the spoiler to destroy.

faqs.question: What does he say angels do?
faqs.answer: He says angels “come to minister to you” and “have a message for you,” and that they are “ministering spirits.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Are they not all ministering spirits sent forth to minister for those who will inherit salvation?

faqs.question: What does he say Satan has authority to do?
faqs.answer: He says Satan has authority to test and tempt mankind, but that obedient believers “have authority over Satan and his fallen angels.”

faqs.question: What does he urge believers to do about Satan?
faqs.answer: He urges “a prayer life,” “a word life” and “a fasting life,” and says it “won’t hurt you to fast once a week.”
